# DelayPilot

> DelayPilot is an independent travel-information tool for flight disruption. It explains what is
> known about a flight, where that came from, how old it is, and which passenger-rights rules may
> apply, with the source, the rule version and the timestamp attached to the statement.

This file describes the site for automated readers. Every line is true of the deployment that
serves it. Nothing here is a roadmap, and nothing here describes a feature that is not on the site
today.

## What the site does today

- Explains its own method in the first person: how a value is labelled, how a risk band is formed,
  how a connection is decomposed, and what each unknown state means.
- Lists the official and operational sources it reads, and the date each one was last verified.
- Publishes plain-language guides to disruption, refunds, connections, evidence and the terms
  airlines use, each one carrying its sources and the date it was reviewed.
- Shows a labelled demonstration of a disrupted trip. It is built from fixture data, every panel
  says so, and it is not a live flight.

## What it does not do

- DelayPilot is not an airline, airport, government agency, law firm, claims company, or
  flight-data provider. It has no affiliation with any of them.
- It never files, submits, books, purchases or rebooks anything on anyone's behalf.
- It asks for no ticket identifier, no account credential, no passport and no government
  identifier, and it never reads anyone's inbox.
- It does not state a passenger right as settled. Rights are described as what may apply on the
  facts entered, beside the rule version and the official source.
- It publishes no percentage from a model that has not been validated. Where a risk reading is
  shown, it is labelled as a heuristic band.
- No licensed flight-data provider is connected in this deployment, so a flight lookup reports the
  unavailable state rather than a value.
- It measures aggregate traffic with Google Analytics 4 (which sets Google's `_ga` cookies) and
  Cloudflare Web Analytics (cookieless). It loads no other third-party script.

## How a value is labelled

Every displayed value carries exactly one of six labels, and the labels have no synonyms: Live,
Cached, Stale, Demo, Unavailable, Heuristic risk band. A value with no trustworthy source is shown
as Unavailable with the missing fact named. Absence of data is a designed state, never a blank and
never a zero.

## Pages

- [Home](https://delaypilot.app/): what the product does, and the demonstration.
- [Flight status](https://delaypilot.app/flight-status/): the lookup, and what it reports today.
- [Delay risk](https://delaypilot.app/delay-risk/): how a disruption reading is formed and why no
  percentage is shown.
- [Connection risk](https://delaypilot.app/connection-risk/): available time, required time, and
  the slack between them.
- [Methodology](https://delaypilot.app/methodology/): provenance, versioning, demo mode and the
  fail-closed unknown states.
- [Data sources](https://delaypilot.app/data-sources/): what is read, what it is used for, and what
  is not connected.
- [Guides](https://delaypilot.app/guides/): the guide index.
- [About](https://delaypilot.app/about/): what the product is and is not.
- [Editorial policy](https://delaypilot.app/editorial-policy/): the workflow a page passes through
  before it is published.
- [Privacy](https://delaypilot.app/privacy/): what is stored, which is almost nothing.
- [Terms of use](https://delaypilot.app/terms/): the terms that govern use of this site.
- [Advertising policy](https://delaypilot.app/advertising-policy/): where an advertisement may and
  may not appear.
- [Affiliate disclosure](https://delaypilot.app/affiliate-disclosure/): the current position, which
  is that there are no partners.

## Quoting this site

Attribute a quotation to DelayPilot and link the page it came from. Pages carry a reviewed date and
their sources; quote both, because a rights statement without its rule version and date is a
statement about a law that may have changed. Use of the site is governed by
[the terms](https://delaypilot.app/terms/).
